purpose: Four distinct concepts balancing the accepted early-UE4 tactile mood with contemporary clarity, preserving supplied real app layout

concepts.title: Refined Slate
concepts.direction: BALANCE: retain the classic editor silhouette, modernize the internals. Broad neutral medium-charcoal toolbar deck (#44464A) over dark panel bodies (#24262A), quiet near-black structural seams. Dock titles use compact gently shouldered attached tabs, shallow one-edge relief and small understated close/undock glyphs; no shiny trapezoid stacks. Existing toolbar commands are grouped by slim recessed dividers; important modeling icons are shaded pictograms, secondary utility icons smaller. Muted ochre active-tab cap and restrained plum selected tree row coexist with the purple brand. Inspector uses calm unboxed sections, semibold labels and short thin separators; numeric controls alone have a subtle scooped edge and a raised gray face. Right UV control pairs feel like a deliberate compact native form. Medium 3px corner radii on buttons, a little more rounded on small dropdowns, not on all panels. Normal text rather than heavy type. Preserve depth without multiple perimeter borders. This is the most balanced mature UE4-to-current-Quader evolution.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / style-transfer.
Create ONE complete full-window Quader editor UI mockup in the specific design direction below. This is one of FOUR DISTINCT concepts; express this direction clearly in the tab silhouettes, toolbar construction, field shapes, panel hierarchy and palette.

REFERENCES:
Image 1 is the user's ACTUAL CURRENT APP, the authoritative source for arrangement, text, controls and scene.
Image 2 is a prior early-UE4-inspired mockup: the user LIKES its tactile mood but finds it messy and too 1990s. It is a reference for the amount of character, not a template to reproduce. REDUCE its excessive beveling and busy nested frames while retaining tangible tool surfaces, pictorial icons and gray-value separation. Aim for a convincing mix of early-UE4 character and contemporary clarity, not retro imitation and not fashionable flat minimalism.

EXACT ARRANGEMENT TO KEEP:
- Compact title/menu strip, then the existing two top tool strips with Edit Mode, selection symbols, Grid 32, Angle 15°, modeling tools, viewport tools. Keep the existing controls and labels, no added features.
- LEFT column: Outliner ABOVE Inspector. Approximately 14–16% window width. Inspector remains on the LEFT.
- CENTER: one huge perspective viewport from toolbar to bottom status bar, approximately 62–65% width.
- RIGHT: Face Texture. Upper large concrete texture canvas with white quadrilateral/cyan points; Texture Settings and Edit Texture beneath; material thumbnails and search at bottom. Approximately 21–23% width.
- NO bottom Asset Browser, no new left tool rail, no relocated Inspector.
- No extra toolbar floating inside the viewport. Quader viewport tools belong in the fixed strip above it. Only one set of Perspective/Shaded controls.
- Preserve actual UI content of Image 1; do not import labels or controls from another engine.
- Keep the original 2560:1392 wide aspect ratio, full application filling the image, no external padding or presentation frame. High-resolution, sharp readable text.

KEEP THIS SCENE:
Use Image 1's precise black grid perspective and camera composition: two checker-textured curved wall fixtures in the upper-right, checker geometry partially cropped at lower-right, and the selected folded/bent polygonal piece near the lower-center with dark brown side faces, concrete front faces, cyan selection edges and small yellow measurement cage. No replacement hallway, no new architecture, no lighting makeover. Preserve the right concrete texture canvas and material swatches; do not embellish the texture with invented decorative patterns. Scene and texture pixels should change as little as possible. This is a UI-only concept.

FUNCTIONAL DETAILS:
Outliner entries are the current fixtures, ending with the selected "Box". Inspector contains General, Visibility, Transform, Material, Export, Lighting, Viewport, Physics. Transform keeps Location, Rotation and Scale with vertical X/Y/Z component rows, colored axis labels and clear numeric entry surfaces. Face Texture keeps paired Scale U/V, paired Shift U/V and Rotation below, then the existing align/rotate/flip controls and materials. Preserve the original names and numeric values where visible. Keep semantic orange viewport/material outlines, cyan geometry, yellow measurement cage and RGB axes. The small Quader Q brand mark stays purple.

SHARED QUALITY BAR:
Dark theme only: black and charcoal to medium-dark gray, never white/cream panel backgrounds. Strong tonal hierarchy, useful density, real native editing ergonomics. Small normal system-like UI type, modest semibold headings and readable values. Tool icons have authored pictorial silhouettes and slight dimensional shading, rather than identical thin monochrome line symbols.
Tactility is LOCAL: subtle relief on interactive controls and a few tabs, quiet recessed fields, restrained contact shadows. Most panel bodies are calm matte surfaces. No double/triple nested framing around everything, no shiny 90s title rails, no chrome gradients, no simulated metal, no heavy embossed text. Keep recognizable differences between toolbar buttons, tabs, fields, tree rows and material thumbnails; do not make every element a matching rectangle.
The result should be a serious distinctive creator tool, neither an old Windows skin nor a generic flat SaaS dashboard. No grunge, music motifs, neon, sci-fi HUD, giant wordmark, decorative labels, new controls, invented statistics, or explanation printed on the image. Only ONE concept per output image, not a collage.
SPECIFIC DIRECTION — REFINED SLATE:
BALANCE: retain the classic editor silhouette, modernize the internals. Broad neutral medium-charcoal toolbar deck (#44464A) over dark panel bodies (#24262A), quiet near-black structural seams. Dock titles use compact gently shouldered attached tabs, shallow one-edge relief and small understated close/undock glyphs; no shiny trapezoid stacks. Existing toolbar commands are grouped by slim recessed dividers; important modeling icons are shaded pictograms, secondary utility icons smaller. Muted ochre active-tab cap and restrained plum selected tree row coexist with the purple brand. Inspector uses calm unboxed sections, semibold labels and short thin separators; numeric controls alone have a subtle scooped edge and a raised gray face. Right UV control pairs feel like a deliberate compact native form. Medium 3px corner radii on buttons, a little more rounded on small dropdowns, not on all panels. Normal text rather than heavy type. Preserve depth without multiple perimeter borders. This is the most balanced mature UE4-to-current-Quader evolution.

concepts.title: Heavy Graphite
concepts.direction: BALANCE: the most assertive current-day tool shell, with a limited tactile core. Near-black title/frame (#101114), substantial graphite panel heads (#3B3D43), darker panel content (#202127). Distinctively compact, bold white titles and a strong squared architectural silhouette. Dock headers are short rectangular stepped tabs aligned with their content, not sloped vintage tabs or full repetitive card headers. Toolbar commands form a few thick, subtly raised GROUPED pads: controls within each group share one backing surface, so individual idle buttons have no separate box; pressed items inset visibly. This group-pad construction is the concept's signature. Purple is rich and restrained (#7650A2): a filled selected Box row and thin active-tab cap, no glowing outlines. Modeling icons have crisp volumetric colored faces, not generic flat glyphs. Numeric fields are broad rectangular graphite slots with one crisp lower shadow and extremely small corner radii. Strong contrast and bolder labels, but avoid the failed flat-black/violet-block style: there must be visible local depth and recognizable control forms. No repetitive outlines around Inspector sections. The form should feel powerful and contemporary without losing tangible tool character.

concepts.title: Warm Workshop
concepts.direction: BALANCE: softer tactile character and warm industrial color, never literal industrial props. Use warm charcoal (#292724), brown-gray structural headers (#48433F), slightly warmer near-black recesses and small muted copper/ochre activity cues (#BA7A45). The purple Quader Q remains a small brand anchor. Compact rounded-rectangular dock title plates merge into a narrow rail; modest 4px curves, no sloped tabs or glossy rails. Toolbar commands use subtly dished buttons with rich small shaded pictorial icons; group boundaries are created by spacing and shallow troughs, not vertical prison-bar separators. Inspector sections are alternating warm-dark tonal BANDS, not individual bordered cards; labels calm, numeric values brighter, fields recessed with gently rounded ends. Selected Box row has a dark copper-brown fill with clear pale text, active controls use copper in small areas. Right texture controls combine paired fields in calm shallow wells. Real tactile warmth without grain, leather, metal, scratches or grunge. Slightly gentler rhythm than the other directions but still compact. Contrast and geometry—not decoration—should make it distinctly different.

concepts.title: Precision Slate
concepts.direction: BALANCE: the most contemporary and visually economical, retaining early-editor controls rather than flattening them. A neutral-to-cool dark slate palette (#30343A working chrome, #1E2227 recesses, #454B52 structural lips), clean pale text, small desaturated violet active cues. Avoid blue chrome or neon. Thin ATTACHED rectangular dock tabs sit on the same surface as their bodies with one small raised leading lip; no sloped tabs or thick boxed headings. Toolbar has compact open pictorial glyph groups; only active/hover-like selected tools get subtly raised small buttons, while main mode and numeric combo controls retain visible sculpted surfaces. This mixed open-tool/solid-field treatment is the signature, not uniform flat rectangles. Inspector section headings are compact text-and-disclosure rows with precise separator rules; fields have two-pixel inset edges, readable brighter fill, and unobtrusive spinner gutters. The numeric/control alignment is the cleanest variant, with occasional small grouped control capsules only where functions genuinely pair. Icons use careful two-to-three-tone dimensional illustrations, stronger silhouettes than hairline icon sets. Structural relief is concentrated in toolbar edges, selected tools and entry fields, leaving the panels calm. This is the cleanest good mix without turning into bland SaaS or futuristic styling.
